Functions of polyamines
Polyamines (putrescine, spermidine, and spermine) are synthesized from arginine- and proline-derived ornithine via ornithine
decarboxylase, spermidine synthase, and spermine synthase in humans (Wu, 2022). Methionine is required for the production
of spermidine and spermine via the formation of S-adenosylmethionine as the methyl group donor. Polyamines are essential
for DNA and protein syntheses, angiogenesis, spermatogenesis, and wound healing (Agostinelli, 2020; Pegg, 2016). Polyamines
also participate in the posttranslational modiﬁcations of some proteins, such as eIF5A by deoxyhypusine synthase to form the hypu-
sine residue that is critical for eukaryotic translation (Park and Wolff, 2018). Furthermore, polyamines are substrates for some trans-
